item.title: OldPadDeck 0.1.9
item.description:
• A menu that reads at a glance. The menu bar and Dock menus now say plainly whether your iPad is there: “iPad connected” or “Waiting for your iPad”.
  • Two things at the first level: Configure Deck and Pair a Device. Everything you set once (Launch at Login, Permissions, Paired Devices, the iPad address, updates, feedback) is under Settings. When an update is waiting, it shows at the top of the menu.
  • Paired Devices shows the devices you use. Older ones can be removed in one click.
  • In Configure Deck, the side bar now runs to the edge of the window, so the window buttons no longer sit on its corner.

item.title: OldPadDeck 0.1.8
item.description:
• The iPad stays paired. On some iPads the deck could come back to the pairing screen and ask for the code again, typically after the Mac had slept, although the Mac still knew the iPad. The iPad now keeps its pairing in a second place and reconnects by itself within seconds.
  • An iPad paired with an earlier version picks this up at its next connection. If it is already showing the pairing screen, type the code one last time (menu bar icon → Pair a Device…).
  • Pairing behaves. The Pair a Device window on the Mac could draw its text and its code on top of each other, and an iPad whose request got no answer stayed on “Pairing…”. The window keeps its layout, and the iPad gives up after a few seconds and lets you type the code again.
  • When the Mac refuses a device, it now notes why in a small local file, to make such problems easier to track down. Nothing leaves your Mac.

item.title: OldPadDeck 0.1.7
item.description:
• OldPadDeck now updates itself. On its second launch, it asks whether to check for new versions automatically (once a day). When one is out, a blue dot appears on its Dock and menu bar icons, and Check for Updates… shows what changed and installs it in one click, then relaunches.
  • The iPad tells you too: a blue dot on the ••• button, and a line in its menu. Tap it to open the update window on the Mac.
  • Every update is signed, and the app refuses one that isn't. The check reads a small file on oldpaddeck.com and sends nothing about your Mac.
  • New on the website: What's new, with every version.
